entities.name: Manuel de Moura, 2nd Marquis of Castelo Rodrigo
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Manuel de Moura, 2nd Marquis of Castelo Rodrigo, played a pivotal role in shaping the Habsburg Netherlands during the 17th century.

As Governor from 1644 to 1647, he oversaw the administration of the Dutch Republic, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Habsburgs and the Dutch.

His tenure was marked by significant economic and political developments, including the establishment of trade agreements and the cultivation of diplomatic relations with key European powers.

The legacy of Manuel de Moura can be seen in the continued prosperity of the Habsburg Netherlands, which remained a major economic hub throughout the 18th century.

"The key to our success lies in our ability to balance the interests of our people with those of our European partners," Manuel de Moura once said, reflecting the pragmatic approach that defined his leadership.
